packet.headline_seed: Hezbollah drone strike videos show evolving tactics against Israel
packet.description_seed: BBC Verify has examined dozens of videos of fibre-optic drone attacks carried out by the Lebanese armed group.

what: Hezbollah drone strike videos show evolving tactics against Israel

clean_source_blocks.text: BBC Verify has examined dozens of videos of fibre-optic drone attacks carried out by the Lebanese armed group.

Hezbollah has increased its use of small first-person view (FPV) drones to attack Israel, including systems controlled by fibre-optic cables to evade sophisticated defences. BBC Verify has geolocated 35 videos shared by the Lebanese armed group since 26 March which show strikes on Israeli soldiers, armoured vehicles and air defence systems in southern Lebanon and northern Israel. Experts told BBC Verify the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has "so far been unable to develop any effective countermeasures", as the small drones can easily bypass detection systems. The drones can also be made from commercially available and 3D-printed components - and are cheap compared to the high-value targets they can destroy, experts also said. The use of cheap FPV drones became widespread during the Russia-Ukraine war and has changed modern warfare.

Hezbollah has been using several types of larger attack drones against targets in northern Israel for many years, Jaber added, but the use of FPVs represents an "entirely different category". BBC Verify has found videos of nearly 100 apparent FPV attacks shared on Hezbollah's Telegram channel since 26 March, 35 of which have been verified. Hezbollah does not appear to have shared any footage of similar strikes from the conflict beginning on 2 March. One verified video shared on Thursday shows at least four FPV drones attacking an Israeli border outpost near Kiryat Shmona, targeting a series of military vehicles in sequence. At least two of them can be seen heavily damaged or destroyed in the clips. BBC Verify has also tracked similar drone strikes in sout ---

One recent strike marked the first reported FPV drone attack on Israeli territory, hitting an area close to the border and injuring several soldiers. Images released by the Israeli military also show caches of quadcopter drones allegedly seized from Hezbollah positions. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has been adapting to the evolving threat, studying Hezbollah’s tactics and adjusting operational procedures. Measures reportedly include deploying additional radar systems, reducing exposure time for helicopters during evacuations, and integrating anti-drone technologies. Analysts also suggest that Hezbollah may be assembling some of these drones locally, rather than importing fully built systems, indicating a growing domestic capability. EFE

[Lähde: BBC World]
Hezbollah has increased its use of small first-person view (FPV) drones to attack Israel, including systems controlled by fibre-optic cables to evade sophisticated defences.

BBC Verify has geolocated 35 videos shared by the Lebanese armed group since 26 March which show strikes on Israeli soldiers, armoured vehicles and air defence systems in southern Lebanon and northern Israel.

Experts told BBC Verify the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has "so far been unable to develop any effective countermeasures", as the small drones can easily bypass detection systems.

The drones can also be made from commercially available and 3D-printed components - and are cheap compared to the high-value targets they can destroy, experts also said.

The use of cheap FPV drones became widespread during the Russia-Ukraine war and has changed modern warfare.

While the Israeli military has not published all casualty details, Israeli media reports indicate four IDF soldiers and one civilian have been killed in FPV strikes, with dozens more injured.

The IDF told BBC Verify it recognises the threat from drones and is investing "significant resources" in improving defences, developing "more effective alert models" and training soldiers for "improving readiness and increasing awareness of the threat".

According to the Institute for National Security Studies, the IDF has also been using FPV drones for several years, currently operating with them in southern Lebanon and against Hamas in Gaza.

Hisham Jaber, a military analyst and former Lebanese army general, told BBC Arabic the FPV drones can be "undetectable by radar" and the "hundreds" of them at Hezbollah's disposal have been used to disable armoured vehicles - including tanks.

At TOI World Desk, our dedicated team of seasoned journalists and passionate writers tirelessly sifts through the vast tapestry of global events to bring you the latest news and diverse perspectives round the clock. With an unwavering commitment to accuracy, depth, and timeliness, we strive to keep you informed about the ever-evolving world, delivering a nuanced understanding of international affairs to our readers. [Lähde: Agencia EFE]
Jerusalem, May 1 (EFE).- Explosive-laden FPV (first-person view) drones – cheap, agile, and hard to intercept – are increasingly being used by Hezbollah in attacks against Israel, raising new challenges for military defenses.

FPV drones are small quadcopters equipped with front-facing cameras that transmit live video to operators wearing goggles, allowing them to guide the device directly to a target in real time.

Typically measuring around 30 centimeters, these drones can be fitted with explosives and used as “kamikaze” weapons, crashing into targets on impact.

According to analysts, they cost between $200 and $1,000, making them significantly cheaper than conventional missiles.

They can be controlled via radio signals over distances of 5 to 15 km or through fiber-optic cables, which extend range but reduce payload capacity and mobility.

Their main advantages include maneuverability, ease of use, and the ability to evade traditional air defense systems designed for larger projectiles.

FPV drones have been widely used in the war between Ukraine and Russia, where both sides deploy them for reconnaissance and strike missions.

Ukraine has become a leading innovator in their use, while Russia has also adopted the technology, often adapting commercial drone models such as those produced by DJI.

In the current hostilities, Hezbollah has stepped up its use of FPV drones, particularly in southern Lebanon and near the Israeli border.

According to Israeli military reports, around a dozen such attacks have been recorded in the past week alone, resulting in the deaths of two Israeli soldiers and a civilian contractor, as well as multiple injuries.

One recent strike marked the first reported FPV drone attack on Israeli territory, hitting an area close to the border and injuring several soldiers.

Images released by the Israeli military also show caches of quadcopter drones allegedly seized from Hezbollah positions.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has been adapting to the evolving threat, studying Hezbollah’s tactics and adjusting operational procedures.

Measures reportedly include deploying additional radar systems, reducing exposure time for helicopters during evacuations, and integrating anti-drone technologies.

Analysts also suggest that Hezbollah may be assembling some of these drones locally, rather than importing fully built systems, indicating a growing domestic capability. EFE

payload.title: Hezbollahin droonivideot kertovat taktiikan muutoksesta Israelia vastaan
payload.summary: BBC:n faktantarkistusyksikön tarkastamat videot viittaavat siihen, että Hezbollah on lisännyt pienten FPV-droonejen käyttöä iskuissa Israelin joukkoja ja sotilaskalustoa vastaan.
payload.content:
BBC:n faktantarkistusyksikön läpikäymät ja paikantamat videot viittaavat siihen, että libanonilainen aseellinen ryhmä Hezbollah on lisännyt pienten FPV-droonejen käyttöä iskuissa Israelia vastaan. Tarkastetuissa videoissa näkyy iskuja israelilaisiin sotilaisiin, panssaroituihin ajoneuvoihin ja ilmatorjuntajärjestelmiin Etelä-Libanonissa ja Pohjois-Israelissa.

## Pienet droonit muuttavat taistelutapaa

Hezbollah on käyttänyt suurempia hyökkäysdrooneja Pohjois-Israeliin kohdistuneissa iskuissa jo vuosien ajan, mutta nyt esiin nousseet FPV-lennokit edustavat asiantuntijoiden mukaan erilaista uhkaa. FPV-droonia ohjataan käyttäjän näkökulmasta, ja osa laitteista voi hyödyntää valokuitukaapelia ohjaukseen.

Tällainen ratkaisu voi vaikeuttaa droonin havaitsemista ja torjuntaa, koska se ei tukeudu samalla tavalla radiotaajuuksiin kuin monet perinteiset kauko-ohjattavat järjestelmät. BBC Verify on paikantanut 35 Hezbollah’n 26. maaliskuuta jälkeen julkaisemaa videota, joissa näkyy iskuja sotilaskohteisiin. Yhteensä ryhmän Telegram-kanavalla on havaittu lähes sata ilmeistä FPV-iskuvideota samalta ajanjaksolta, mutta niistä vain osa on vahvistettu.

Yhdessä torstaina julkaistussa ja vahvistetussa videossa ainakin neljä FPV-droonia hyökkää israelilaiseen raja-asemaan Kiryat Shmonan lähellä. Videoilla droonit näyttävät kohdistuvan peräkkäin useisiin sotilasajoneuvoihin, joista ainakin kaksi vaurioituu pahoin tai tuhoutuu.

## Torjunta on vaikeaa ja kustannussuhde huolestuttaa

Asiantuntijoiden mukaan pienet FPV-drooni-iskut ovat Israelin puolustusvoimille hankala torjuttava, koska droonit voivat ohittaa kehittyneitä valvonta- ja puolustusjärjestelmiä. Samalla ne ovat suhteellisen halpoja verrattuna kohteisiin, joita niillä voidaan vaurioittaa tai tuhota.

Laitteita voidaan koota kaupallisesti saatavilla olevista ja 3D-tulostetuista osista. Arvioiden mukaan Hezbollah saattaa myös koota osan drooneista paikallisesti sen sijaan, että se toisi valmiita järjestelmiä ulkomailta. Tämä viittaisi kasvavaan kykyyn tuottaa tai muokata drooneja omiin tarpeisiin.

Israelin armeijan kerrotaan mukauttaneen toimintaansa uhan vuoksi. Toimiin on kuulunut muun muassa lisätutkien käyttöönottoa, helikopterien altistusajan lyhentämistä evakuoinneissa sekä droonien torjuntaan tarkoitettujen teknologioiden lisäämistä. Israelin armeijan julkaisemissa kuvissa on myös näkynyt nelikopteridrooneja, joiden se sanoo löytyneen Hezbollah’n asemista.

Halpojen FPV-droonejen yleistyminen sai vauhtia Venäjän ja Ukrainan sodassa, jossa ne ovat muuttaneet nykyaikaista taistelukenttää. Nyt sama kehitys näkyy myös Israelin ja Hezbollah’n välisessä konfliktissa, jossa pienet droonit voivat tuottaa suurta sotilaallista painetta suhteellisen vähäisillä kustannuksilla.
summary_bullets: Hezbollah on lisännyt pienten FPV-droonejen käyttöä iskuissa Israelin joukkoja ja sotilaskalustoa vastaan.
BBC Verify on paikantanut 35 videota, joissa näkyy Hezbollah’n 26. maaliskuuta jälkeen julkaisemia iskuja.
Asiantuntijoiden mukaan valokuituohjatut ja edullisesti koottavat droonit voivat vaikeuttaa Israelin torjuntatoimia.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu packetin vahvistettuihin tietoihin BBC Verifyn geopaikannetuista videoista ja EFE:n täydentäviin tietoihin. Lähdetekstin katkennut kohta jätettiin pois eikä sen pohjalta tehty tarkkoja väitteitä.

article.source_text:
BBC Verify has examined dozens of videos of fibre-optic drone attacks carried out by the Lebanese armed group.

Hezbollah has increased its use of small first-person view (FPV) drones to attack Israel, including systems controlled by fibre-optic cables to evade sophisticated defences. BBC Verify has geolocated 35 videos shared by the Lebanese armed group since 26 March which show strikes on Israeli soldiers, armoured vehicles and air defence systems in southern Lebanon and northern Israel. Experts told BBC Verify the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has "so far been unable to develop any effective countermeasures", as the small drones can easily bypass detection systems. The drones can also be made from commercially available and 3D-printed components - and are cheap compared to the high-value targets they can destroy, experts also said. The use of cheap FPV drones became widespread during the Russia-Ukraine war and has changed modern warfare.

Hezbollah has been using several types of larger attack drones against targets in northern Israel for many years, Jaber added, but the use of FPVs represents an "entirely different category". BBC Verify has found videos of nearly 100 apparent FPV attacks shared on Hezbollah's Telegram channel since 26 March, 35 of which have been verified. Hezbollah does not appear to have shared any footage of similar strikes from the conflict beginning on 2 March. One verified video shared on Thursday shows at least four FPV drones attacking an Israeli border outpost near Kiryat Shmona, targeting a series of military vehicles in sequence. At least two of them can be seen heavily damaged or destroyed in the clips. BBC Verify has also tracked similar drone strikes in sout ---

One recent strike marked the first reported FPV drone attack on Israeli territory, hitting an area close to the border and injuring several soldiers. Images released by the Israeli military also show caches of quadcopter drones allegedly seized from Hezbollah positions. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has been adapting to the evolving threat, studying Hezbollah’s tactics and adjusting operational procedures. Measures reportedly include deploying additional radar systems, reducing exposure time for helicopters during evacuations, and integrating anti-drone technologies. Analysts also suggest that Hezbollah may be assembling some of these drones locally, rather than importing fully built systems, indicating a growing domestic capability. EFE
